## 10. Concern's object and the grounds of its correction

6 October 2026. The named connection is **a formed concern's relation to its object → ethical quality within the unfolding → warranted correction of that concern**. Sections 3 and 7 already reject identifying goodness with successful internal targets. Section 9 preserves a more specific good jointly constituted by informed concern and actual engagement. [Warranted attention, §53](HUIGEN-SELF-GROUND-AUDIT.md#53-warranted-attention-within-a-shared-perspective), already allows improvement without changed outward conduct. The present extension tests the quality of an orientation while holding the other's suffering fixed; it does not rediscover that successful cruelty can be bad.

### Preserve the good activity and isolate the orientation

Two participants genuinely make music together: each hears, answers and shapes the other's contribution, and both understand and care about this engagement. A third person independently undergoes a severe, still-unwanted burden. Compare two continuations retaining the collaboration, its skilled exercise and fulfillment, the third person's burden and subsequent history, and the participants' relevant factual understanding. In one, their enjoyment concerns the shared expression. In the other, enjoyment is also directed toward the third person's undergoing **because it is adverse for that person**.

The comparison matches pleasant intensity and duration and relevant further effects, rather than stipulating equal complete welfare or equal ethical quality. Extra injury, humiliation, changed future aggression, false beliefs about desert, and different opportunities to help cannot supply the alleged contrast. These are conceptual controls to establish, not an observed experiment or a claim that perfectly matched populations can be engineered. Both participants can accurately judge the burden undeserved while welcoming it. Their intentional objects differ, so their complete experiences are not declared identical.

The common collaboration remains actual. Hostile enjoyment does not make its every skill, pleasure or fulfilled concern fictitious. Conversely, its factual accuracy establishes neither the ethical quality of its object nor that of the orientation toward it. An existing desire can succeed without thereby vindicating what it welcomes.

### A positive reason for correction, and a genuine rival

Our affirmative proposal is that **an independently warranted adverse aspect gives a ground against welcoming that very aspect as fulfillment**. The proposed defect concerns the relation now realized, even without another injury caused by it. This is an ethical claim about the response to an identified condition; it is not an inference from a negative signal or from the fact that another person dislikes something.

The supporting explanation is object-specific. Here the feature that makes the orientation satisfied is precisely a feature adverse to an actual life. Criticism answers that orientation's taking the adversity as its welcome object, while leaving other pleasures and achievements available for recognition. If the object instead were the person's relief, or merely a fictional performance understood as such, this particular criticism would need reassessment. If adversity or the attitude's object was misidentified, its stated ground would fail. This makes the proposal answerable to the relation, rather than to an observer's bare disapproval of unfamiliar enjoyment.

Nor does the proposal require the participants to misdescribe the facts. They may know exactly what occurs. The proposed correction concerns how their orientation responds to that condition. To identify it as unfitting is to defend a normative connection, not to correct a false belief by definition. Calling every factually informed preference authoritative would leave no room to assess the orientation on those grounds; its successful formation cannot settle its own authority.

A purely hedonistic account of whole quality can accept the actual pain, all matched pleasures and the genuine collaboration while denying any additional ethical defect in this causally ineffective hostility. It does not merely give a conceded defect less weight. Our judgment favors the object-sensitive account because it explains why the way an adverse life-condition is welcomed can itself be objectionable, even when no additional effect follows. The rival can reject that judgment; neither causal description nor absence of an alternative explanation proves our account necessary. A reply that counts only later harm has not yet addressed the specified present relation.

A second dispute concerns how retained pleasantness participates in the whole. One account retains a favorable component alongside an adverse orientation; another regards that pleasantness as constitutively involved in the defect without independently favoring production of the malicious whole. The [new primary comparisons](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#9-attitudes-to-realized-good-and-adversity) explain this difference. Recognizing actual enjoyment does not decide between these ethical structures. The present argument claims the object-sensitive defect without making either decomposition a foundational axiom or identifying intrinsic-value vocabulary with a proved good-for theory.

### Correction need not eliminate the person or every enjoyment

Where a feasible, independently permissible change redirects enjoyment toward the retained expression, it can improve the orientation in this respect. Actual pleasure, engagement, capacities and personal continuity might remain. Their preservation must be established rather than guaranteed by naming the change correction. The earlier hostile concern ceases or changes; it is not fulfilled by secretly substituting a different object. Costs, coercion, other commitments and subsequent effects remain part of the whole comparison.

The proposed reason is to change the hostile relation, not to annihilate the bearer or suppress all positive affect. It does not depend on a later reward for a reformer or on the third person eventually helping the collaborators. Yet improvement of orientation is not automatically increased welfare for its bearer, an overall ranking, a duty to undertake every correction, or permission to impose it. Any claimed loss in changing the concern needs assessment, not dismissal solely because its former object was adverse.

### Connect actual attitudes to the future-good appraisal

This gives the integral a further kind of proposed content. A caring or hostile orientation can be an actual feature of a history, whose ethical character depends on its object. Its proposed value is different from its instrumental significance through what it later produces. The [recursion distinction](FUTURE-GOOD-INTEGRAL.md#attitudes-as-realizations-rather-than-repeated-future-value) preserves that difference. Neither repeated description of one attitude nor the possibility of caring about caring establishes additional instantiated attitudes. A future benefit also cannot be counted again as fresh present good merely because someone aims at it. A distinct relational contribution requires its own identification and warrant.

The bounded advance is a defended account of why a generated priority can require correction despite factual accuracy and fulfillment, with a rival denying the proposed relational contribution. This concerns the ethical character of formed evaluation itself. It does not supply the original warrant for all goods and burdens, derive a complete ordering, or discharge the universal minimum. The rival can retain ordinary relief reasons while denying this additional defect, so the latter must not become an unannounced prerequisite for baseline concern. The governing whole-process foundation and no-assumptions objective remain open. No new Lean premise, axiom or empirical result is added.

## 9. Attitudes to realized good and adversity

6 October 2026. Primary comparisons for [the concern-correction test](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction). The earlier Moore, Aristotle and Heathwood readings remain inherited. These sources add explanatory alternatives, not independent ethical validation. Both accesses are link-only; no original source bytes or preservation hashes are claimed.

**Thomas Hurka, “Moore in the Middle,” Ethics 113(3), 599–628 (April 2003), DOI 10.1086/345624, [author-hosted published PDF](https://thomashurka.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/moore-in-the-middle1.pdf).** Root and the source contributor read selected extracted passages on printed pp. 605–607, 618–619, 622–623 and 627–628. This is not a complete-article reading; surfaced intervening passages and cited works are not independently relied on.

**Bounded synopsis:** Hurka distinguishes unchanged component value plus additional whole value from value varying with context. His recursive principles appraise attitudes by their fit to their objects and begin with assumed first-order goods and evils. Concern for an unrealized good can itself have value; actual successful contribution can add a distinct relation. He treats these principles as structural explanations rather than derivations of their starting values from more fundamental claims. His skepticism about foundational alternatives is a philosophical judgment, not an impossibility proof. The paper's intrinsic-value vocabulary is not automatically a contemporary welfare account.

**Johan Brännmark, “Good-making and organic unity,” Philosophical Studies 174, 1499–1516 (2017), [publisher full text and DOI](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11098-016-0769-1).** First online 3 September 2016. The source contributor read the complete publisher main text and notes 1–21; root read the abstract, the malicious-pleasure discussion in §4 and notes 19–21, with selected opening context. No cited works, facsimile or empirical evidence were checked.

**Bounded synopsis:** Brännmark proposes that a component's inherent value can help constitute a complex whole without independently favoring its production. Malicious pleasure is his example: its pleasantness can participate in what makes the orientation defective. He contrasts this embedding account with both adding a larger negative value and simply removing the pleasure's value. Different decompositions can remain possible; he acknowledges reliance on evaluative judgments. This supplies a substantive rival to automatic transfer of component value into a promotion reason, not a proved verdict about every relief case or an adopted theory of parthood.

**Our use:** separate a condition's ethical character, the character of an actual orientation toward it, its consequences, and a reason to produce or change the resulting whole. Normative recursion over actual attitudes differs from causal Bellman or production recursion. Neither form of recursion vindicates its evaluative starting content by itself. Counting only actually identified relations, avoiding duplicate attribution of future benefits, and preserving the fixed third-party history are our application controls, not new theorems attributed to either source. The concern-correction argument remains a substantive judgment under assessment.

## 10. Review: concern's object and correction

The [new argument](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction) continues the inherited successful-cruelty question through a stronger fixed-victim comparison. The shared activity remains genuine; pleasant intensity and duration are controlled without matching complete experiential content, welfare or moral value. The third person's actual burden and later history remain fixed. Additional injury, humiliation, changed future aggression and false desert beliefs cannot substitute for the alleged present defect.

The disputed bridge is that adverse realization can make welcoming that very feature unfitting. This is a claim about the existence of an object-sensitive ethical contribution. The hedonistic rival denies that contribution rather than merely giving it a smaller weight. A factually accurate hostile orientation therefore remains a serious case: correction cannot be redescribed as removal of factual error. The affirmative account must defend its proposed relation to the actual adversity.

The argument supplies object-specific support and revision conditions. It retains real pleasure and collaboration while leaving open whether their ethical structure is additive, context-sensitive or embedded in the whole. A proposed redirection changes the hostile concern; it cannot both retain its old satisfaction condition and claim that benign expression fulfills it. Actual preservation of other goods, feasible means and authority need independent warrant. Improvement in the orientation is not automatically welfare improvement or an overall ordering.

The [new source record](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#9-attitudes-to-realized-good-and-adversity) distinguishes structural recursive explanation from causal production, and component value from an automatic reason to promote its containing whole. It records bounded readings, not proof of either theory. Repeated descriptions do not instantiate endless higher-order attitudes; instrumental future benefit cannot be awarded a second time merely because a present concern aims at it.

This remains a bounded whole-quality inquiry. An account can reject the additional relational defect while retaining the contributory minimum, so resolving this extension is not a prerequisite for baseline concern. The comparison still advances the current correction-of-generated-evaluation question by identifying the proposed ground and a rival denying it. It establishes neither universal ethical necessity nor an assumption-free root. No code change or new empirical run is claimed. Exact integration review and file checks are recorded in [the edit receipt](CONCERN-OBJECT-EDITS.json) and [verification](CONCERN-OBJECT-CHECKS.json).

## Attitudes as realizations rather than repeated future value

The [concern-correction comparison](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction) tests whether an actual orientation toward good or adversity contributes to the history's ethical quality, even with further effects fixed. This differs from §5's causal continuation equation and §9's reproductive contribution. Those operators describe what enables or follows what; a normative recursion instead proposes that the ethical character of an actual attitude depends partly on its object. Its starting values and that dependence still need justification.

For the whole-history appraisal G, the practical implication is precise. If a present caring relationship is independently warranted as a good, its actual realization can matter before its hoped-for benefit occurs. The benefit, when realized, is another occurrence; the concern's instrumental value-to-go is not an additional copy of it. Equally, merely redescribing concern as concern-about-good, then as a worthy concern, does not instantiate further attitudes to be counted. Actual formation and the proposed relational contribution need identification. No automatic infinite series of higher-order goods follows.

The relation may also change how component value participates in the whole. Retaining actual pleasantness does not settle whether it supplies a separate favorable term in the appraisal of malicious enjoyment. The [primary comparisons](WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#9-attitudes-to-realized-good-and-adversity) preserve distinct accounts; none is installed as an aggregation axiom. Temporal integration remains a representation of the defended whole appraisal, not a way to decide those ethical relations. This extends the contents to be explained by the generative account without proving a universal favorable direction.

edits.new:
### When fulfilled concern itself needs correction

The [new whole-relation test](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction) retains genuine collaboration and pleasure while holding another person's independently occurring suffering fixed. It asks whether welcoming that suffering precisely as adverse introduces an ethical defect despite causing no further harm. The affirmative proposal gives its ground in how the orientation answers that actual condition; a hedonistic rival denies the additional defect. Factual accuracy cannot decide this normative disagreement.

A warranted redirection could retain the participants and their expressive engagement while changing the hostile concern. It would not fulfill that old concern by substituting a new object. Feasibility, retained goods and permissible means must be established; improvement in this respect is neither an automatic welfare gain nor a complete verdict. Actual enjoyment also does not settle whether its value independently favors producing the malicious whole.

The [integral connection](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/FUTURE-GOOD-INTEGRAL.md#attitudes-as-realizations-rather-than-repeated-future-value) distinguishes value proposed for actual orientations from their causal contribution to future goods. Neither duplicate descriptions nor instrumental forecasts create extra realized goods. The inquiry advances the appraisal of generated priorities while retaining the first-order and relational ethical premises as unresolved. It does not make this stronger whole-quality judgment a prerequisite for baseline concern or complete the universal minimum.

### The next derivation

# Current theory and research

**Correcting fulfilled concern, 6 October 2026:** [the new whole-relation argument](_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-ARGUMENT.md#10-concerns-object-and-the-grounds-of-its-correction) tests a generated orientation's ethical quality while holding third-party suffering and further effects fixed. It defends redirecting enjoyment of adversity toward retained genuine engagement, with factual accuracy, real pleasure and a hedonistic rival preserved. [Primary comparisons](_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/WHOLE-PROCESS-REALIZATION-SOURCES.md#9-attitudes-to-realized-good-and-adversity) distinguish recursive attitude appraisal from causal production and component value from a reason to promote its whole. **Next:** vindicate or revise the proposed object-sensitive ground without assuming that every retained benefit automatically supplies such a reason. This supports the governing correction-of-evaluation inquiry; it is not a new prerequisite for the contributory minimum or completed universal grounding.
